data.name: Keen: One Girl Army
data.detailed_description:
Keen is a sliding puzzle game with turn-by-turn tactical combat and a hint of adventure!​

Guide Kim, a grumpy little girl raised by her grandmother to save the world on her journey to stop an evil secret society from destroying her village. Innovative controls and fluid gameplay allow players to choose their own pace, whether fast as a hack'n'slash or methodic as chess. It’s fresh gameplay to a classic genre - moving and attacking are the same thing!





Kim is a lovely 8 year old girl that lives in a peaceful insular island with her grandmother. Abandoned by her mother not long after birth, she must put grievances aside to focus on something of utter importance - Kim is the youngest descendant of a lineage of female warriors and her training is about to begin. The pink heart on the cheeks is their birthmark and the protection of Village, their duty. Following a trail of brainwashed minions and high-tech robot soldiers, she would soon find herself in the middle of a world-domination plot carried on by an evil secret society!





Keen's main innovation lies in its turn-based movement and attack mechanics. Slide our tiny hero vertically and horizontally to move her around puzzly rooms, or to slash through enemies with her mighty blade. Combat relies on precision-planning of enemy placement - a fresh take on the tactics genre.

  • 6+hours Of Non-filler Content
  • Unveil Kim's story as she tries to save the day!
  • Discover secret items, unlock secret levels and get special powers!
  • Slash your way through several unique enemies! Also...boss battles!
  • BIG, maze-like dungeons, spanning from mysterious forests to top-secret underwater labs!

reviews.review:
Keen: One Girl Army is a clever puzzle-adventure that takes a familiar grid-based dungeon structure and gives it a distinctive tactical identity. Developed by Cat Nigiri and published by Phoenixx Inc. and 2P Games, the game centers on Kim, a remarkably capable eight-year-old warrior whose seemingly peaceful life becomes entangled with a much larger threat. Instead of relying on conventional action combat, the experience combines sliding movement, turn-based encounters, exploration, and environmental puzzles into a compact adventure that rewards planning more than quick reflexes.

Kim belongs to a lineage of female warriors tasked with protecting their village, recognizable through a pink heart-shaped birthmark. Raised by her grandmother after being abandoned by her mother, she has been trained for responsibilities far beyond those expected of an ordinary child. Her abilities are soon put to the test as she confronts brainwashed enemies, dangerous robots, and a mysterious organization with ambitions for world domination. The premise is deliberately exaggerated and playful, giving the adventure the energy of an animated action series while still leaving room for a few more personal elements surrounding Kim and her family.

The defining feature is the unusual movement system. Kim does not simply walk around the grid one square at a time. Selecting a direction sends her sliding across the available space, and this same movement principle becomes part of attacking enemies. Consequently, every room is effectively a tactical puzzle. Players need to determine where Kim will travel, where she will eventually stop, which enemies can be struck along the way, and whether her resulting position will leave her vulnerable. What initially seems like a restrictive movement mechanic gradually reveals itself as the foundation for nearly every strategic decision.

Because encounters are turn-based, the game encourages careful observation rather than frantic input. Players can examine enemy positions and think through a sequence before acting. This produces a satisfying rhythm in which a complicated room may initially look chaotic, only to become surprisingly elegant once the correct sequence is discovered. Successfully cutting through enemies in a carefully planned chain of movements is especially rewarding because the solution feels earned through understanding rather than reflexes.

Exploration gives the mechanic enough variety to support a broader adventure. Kim travels through large maze-like dungeons and contrasting environments, including natural areas and technologically advanced locations such as hidden underwater facilities. The stages contain optional discoveries, secret areas, collectibles, and special challenges that encourage players to investigate beyond the most obvious route. New abilities and changing environmental arrangements gradually complicate the puzzles, helping the central sliding concept remain interesting as the campaign progresses.

Combat benefits from the same thoughtful design. Enemies are more than objects that simply need to be eliminated because their locations determine how safely Kim can move through each encounter. Different combinations of opponents create increasingly complicated spatial problems, and bosses provide larger tests of the player's understanding of movement and positioning. A poorly chosen attack can leave Kim somewhere inconvenient, while a well-planned sequence can dismantle a threatening group with impressive efficiency.

The visual presentation supports the game's playful personality. Its colorful top-down environments, expressive characters, and cartoon-inspired designs contrast nicely with the more dangerous elements of Kim's mission. Robots and sinister conspiracies might sound like ingredients for a grim adventure, but the game generally maintains a light and energetic atmosphere. This makes it approachable while still giving its environments and enemies enough personality to keep the journey visually engaging.

Its focused length also works in its favor. The adventure does not attempt to transform its central concept into an enormous campaign filled with unnecessary systems. Instead, it concentrates on progressively more demanding applications of sliding, attacking, exploration, and positioning. Hidden content and achievements provide additional objectives for players who enjoy completion, while those primarily interested in solving the main puzzles can progress without excessive distractions.

The biggest potential weakness is also inseparable from the game's central strength. Sliding movement deliberately removes much of the freedom found in ordinary action adventures. Reaching a seemingly nearby position can require several calculated moves, and players who prefer direct control may occasionally find this frustrating. The narrative is also more functional than deeply developed, with the mechanical puzzle design providing the strongest reason to continue. Anyone expecting extensive RPG systems, elaborate character development, or reflex-heavy sword combat should adjust those expectations accordingly.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially marked as Steam Deck Verified. The game was originally designed around straightforward directional controls and relatively modest hardware demands, making its turn-based puzzle structure conceptually suitable for handheld play, but the absence of an official Verified designation means complete compatibility should not be assumed. Individual Steam Deck configurations or Proton versions may produce different results, so it is best regarded as a title without guaranteed official Deck verification rather than presented as fully certified.

Overall, Keen: One Girl Army is a focused and imaginative puzzle adventure that understands the value of building an entire experience around one strong mechanic. Its combination of sliding movement and turn-based combat creates surprisingly deep positional puzzles without requiring complicated controls. Maze-like stages, secrets, unusual enemies, bosses, and a charming protagonist provide enough variety around that foundation to make the journey feel complete. It is particularly easy to recommend to players who enjoy spatial puzzles, deliberate strategy, and games that transform simple rules into increasingly demanding challenges.

Rating: 8/10
